label: voteLockOpen: the cs.closed half of the quality terminal test is dropped
why: A DELIBERATE SURVIVOR: closed and a live quality row cannot coexist, so no test can catch this. cs.closed is written only by CloseDeadClaim, which refuses a claim with an answer ('it settles, it does not die'), and every route into the quality lane needs an answered claim. That refusal is pinned by TestQualityLockReleasesWhenItsVoteCanNoLongerDecideAnything, which asserts exactly that message. The term stays because it is the terminal test and a terminal test that only half-checks terminality is a trap for the next lane that ends a claim a new way — which is what arm 5 of check-epoch-coherence counts writers for. IF THIS COMES BACK CAUGHT, some path now closes an answered claim: promote it and delete this note.

label: voteLockOpen: carry-forward keeps only its qualityReasked half
why: A DELIBERATE SURVIVOR, redundant by implication: qualityReasked implies slotConsumed, so dropping the slotConsumed half changes nothing. reaskQualityTally sets qualityReasked only AFTER its `if !cs.slotConsumed` early return, and CounterFlag sets it behind a pending slash, which only a conclusive flag creates. Both tests that build a carry-forward state assert the two flags together (TestQualityLockHoldsWhenTheTallyCarriesIntoLaterRounds and TestTheCounterLaneHoldsCoinAndItsRedundancyIsTheReasonWhy), so the implication is pinned even though the term is not. Kept because the predicate should say what it means — the condition IS reaskQualityTally's, and writing half of it would make the two drift silently. IF THIS COMES BACK CAUGHT, qualityReasked is now reachable without slotConsumed: promote it and delete this note.

label: votingWeight: the negative clamp is dropped
why: A DELIBERATE SURVIVOR: w is min of two non-negative reads, so the clamp cannot fire and no test can catch its removal. PastVotes returns a checkpointed balance and BalanceOf a live one; neither goes negative — grc20votes checks sufficiency on every move and nothing burns from a user's balance, which arm 7 of check-epoch-coherence counts. The clamp stays because the thing that would make it reachable is a burn taking coin out from under a holder, and lock.gno's spendable() carries the same defensive clamp for the same anticipated case with a comment saying it is not reachable today. IF THIS COMES BACK CAUGHT, a negative weight has become reachable: promote it and go read arm 7.

label: lockVote: a zero-weight row is recorded instead of skipped
why:
A DELIBERATE SURVIVOR found by an operator-level sweep of voteweight.gno, votelock.gno and lock.gno — eleven mechanical mutations of comparison and boolean operators, of which this was the only one to survive. amount is never non-positive here: all three lockVote call sites refuse a non-positive weight before reaching it (the governor's castVote panics on w <= 0, and approve and VoteQuality each panic on both a zero snapshot and a zero live figure), so the guard cannot fire. Its removal would record an open row of weight 0, which contributes nothing to voteLockedOf's max and is cleared by the next prune — a cleanliness cost, not a safety one, which is why no test sees it. Kept because a lock function that will silently write a meaningless row is a worse primitive than one that will not. IF THIS COMES BACK CAUGHT, some lane now locks a non-positive weight and that lane's own w <= 0 guard is what to read.

VERIFIED AGAIN LATER, and the 'all three call sites' phrasing needed sharpening: two of them refuse the weight THEY pass, and the third refuses a different quantity. modvote.gno and quality.gno both test `w <= 0` on the value handed to lockVote. dispute.gno guards `held := voteCap(...)` and then passes `dw`, which it reads back from the governor after VoteWithCap — a different number. dw is still positive, but by p/governor's castVote, which panics on `w <= 0` ('no voting power at that epoch') and then takes min(w, cap) with cap = held > 0. So the third site's protection lives in ANOTHER PACKAGE, and the claim is transitive rather than local.

THAT LAYER IS ITSELF PINNED, which is what makes the transitivity safe to rely on: the main corpus carries `castVote: a zero-weight address may vote` (`if w <= 0` -> `if w < 0`), caught. If that row ever left the corpus, this row would stop being INVALID and become a live survivor with money attached — a zero-weight vote lock. Call-site COUNT re-measured too: still exactly three, after two new subsystems landed next door.

label: accrueSegment: the pause's senior conjunct compares > instead of >=
why: INVALID, NOT A SURVIVOR: the conjunct is implied by the one before it, so the two operators agree on every reachable state. accrueSegment has already returned unless curPeriodBudget > 0, so rMax = rMaxPeriods x curPeriodBudget > 0; the first conjunct then requires reservoirR() > 0, which requires cumAccrual - reservedTail - juniorReserved > 0 through both clamps, hence cumAccrual > reservedTail. MEASURED as well as argued: a probe panicking on the deciding state (first conjunct true AND cumAccrual == reservedTail) fired ZERO times across the whole kourtv2 suite. The conjunct is kept because rMaxPeriods is a dial - at 0 the first conjunct is vacuously true and this becomes the only thing still accruing for a waiting senior. IF THIS EVER COMES BACK CAUGHT, either rMax gained a floor or reservoirR stopped clamping: re-derive the implication before promoting it.

label: PullSenior: a zero payment is paid, emitted and counted
why: VALID BUT UNREACHABLE BY ANY HARNESS THIS REPO HAS, which is a different thing from a survivor. pay is never negative (covered is monotone in cumAccrual and clamped to the amount, and paid only ever rises to meet it), so the guard fires exactly at pay == 0. Dropping it changes NO state: e.paid += 0, seniorOwed -= 0, seniorPaid += 0, mintEmission returns on its own amount <= 0 guard, and the function returns 0 either way. The single difference is a spurious SeniorPaid event carrying paid=0 - and events are exactly what emission.gno's header says clients index to build the 'what am I owed' view, so the noise is real. THE REASON THIS ROW GIVES CHANGED ONCE THE EVENT FACILITY LANDED, and the old one is kept here because it was the wrong reason: it said no event accessor exists anywhere. A _test.gno still cannot read events, but a _filetest.gno CAN - the `Events:` directive matches the run's whole event stream, and z_events_filetest.gno has used it since the mod-log commit. Two candidate objections were measured and BOTH failed: the event block would not be unwieldy (the realm has 11 chain.Emit sites in total and quality.gno, crystallize.gno and answer.gno emit nothing at all, so a senior path emits a handful), and a pull needs no elapsed time either (right after enqueueSenior, start = reservedTail + juniorReserved >= cumAccrual, so the FIRST pull already pays zero). WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS IT is the height. Every route into enqueueSenior - the dispute comp, the crystallize carrot, the flag bounty - passes a voting or settlement window, and a filetest cannot advance the clock: EnableTestClock is deployer-gated and a filetest is never the deployer, which z_testclock_filetest.gno asserts as its own subject ('only the deployer may drive the test clock'). So no senior entitlement can be brought into existence inside a filetest, and the one harness that IS the deployer - the txtar suite - cannot see events: no txtar in gnoland/testdata asserts one and the runner does not surface them. Kept because a crank anyone may call must not emit a payment that did not happen. PROMOTE THIS when either lever appears: a filetest able to reach a senior entitlement at a fixed height, or event assertions in the txtar harness (which make-check now runs).

label: WithdrawBonus: the zero-conviction guard needs BOTH to be zero
why: INVALID BY UNREACHABILITY, not a survivor. The two forms can only differ where exactly one operand is non-positive. convCC == 0 with a positive pool: the mutant proceeds and mulDiv128 returns 0, capBonus floors it at 0, mintEmission returns on its own guard - the same 0. convCC > 0 with a zero pool: the mutant divides by zero, but that state cannot exist, because the caller has already panicked unless side == provisional, so this position's conviction is PART of winPoolConvCC (= midGross of the winning side). MEASURED both ways: a probe panicking on `convCC > 0 && winPoolConvCC <= 0` fired ZERO times across the suite, and a companion probe on `convCC > 0` fired, so the line is genuinely exercised and the zero is not vacuous. Kept because it is the only thing standing between a zero-conviction winning side and a division by zero when BOTH are zero - which is reachable, and which both forms handle.

label: PullCarrot: the zero-weight guard needs BOTH to be zero
why: INVALID BY UNREACHABILITY, same shape as the WithdrawBonus guard above. w == 0 with a positive denominator gives share 0 through mulDiv128 and returns 0 at the `share <= 0` floor either way. w > 0 with a zero denominator would divide by zero and cannot happen: on the decided path denom is cs.carrotDenom, the winning side's tally on the deciding round, and the block above has already panicked unless this voter's recorded choice EQUALS carrotChoice, so w is one of that sum's terms; on the conclusive path denom is conclusiveTurnout and w is this voter's weight within it. MEASURED: a probe on `w > 0 && denom <= 0` fired ZERO times, and a companion probe on `w > 0` fired, so the line is exercised. Kept for the reachable both-zero case.

label: AuthorBonus: the second seeded gate is dropped
why: A DELIBERATE SURVIVOR, and its own comment already says why: the draw is zeroed at crystallize, so this is belt-and-braces, asserted at the payout site because that is where a future change would most plausibly break it. It cannot fire today - drawAuthor is 0 on every seeded claim, so dropping the gate falls through to capBonus(0, ...) = 0 and pays the same nothing. MEASURED: a probe panicking on `cs.seeded && cs.drawAuthor != 0` fired ZERO times across the suite, while a companion probe on `cs.seeded` alone fired, so AuthorBonus IS reached with a seeded claim and the first probe's silence is about the state, not about coverage. The crystallize-time gate that makes it redundant IS pinned, by both `the author slice is zeroed for every UNSEEDED claim` and `P7: the author slice is not paid`. IF THIS COMES BACK CAUGHT, a seeded claim now carries an author draw: read I5 in MODERATION.md section 8 before promoting it.

label: ClaimSeries: the merge advances the side that did NOT change at this epoch
why: NOT A SURVIVOR AND NOT A CATCH - THIS ONE HANGS. The merge loop advances i only inside `if i < len(ys) && ys[i].e == e`, and `e` is the min of the two heads, so unmutated at least one side always matches and an index always moves. Inverting the test makes the matching side the one that does NOT advance: neither index moves, `e` never changes, and the loop appends rows for ever. A hang cannot be caught, because catching needs the suite to finish and say so. mutate.py bounds every suite with SUITE_TIMEOUT (600s, MUTATE_SUITE_TIMEOUT to override) and reports a row that reaches it as TIMED OUT, counted with the non-results - so this row is classified rather than silently mistaken for either outcome. It stays here as the answer to 'why is that operator not pinned', and it is not in the corpus because a full pass should not spend a ten-minute timeout re-observing a bound that selftest-checks.py already tests. ONE REFINEMENT worth keeping: the non-termination is not in the loop CONDITION, it is in the loop's ADVANCE guard, so 'skip mutations of for-statements' would not have caught this - two independent sweeps hit it, at ten and fifty-six minutes. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 and the status HOLDS: still [timed out] at MUTATE_SUITE_TIMEOUT=120. Note that `make gaps` filters `slow` rows out, and a KNOWN-GAPS row is not in the main corpus either, so this row is measured in NEITHER direction — its status is a claim, not an observation, until somebody re-runs it. To do that: strip `slow` into a scratch batch and run mutate-parallel with MUTATE_SUITE_TIMEOUT set low. Not automated because bounding these needs a PER-ROW timeout — a global 120s would spuriously fail normal rows, one of which timed out at 600s under 4-shard load — and two rows do not justify that plumbing.

label: qualifiedSymbol: a court symbol is rendered unsanitised
why: INVALID BY ALPHABET, not a survivor. qualifiedSymbol wraps the coin symbol in InlineText and the wrap cannot change the output: courtSymbol is strings.ToUpper(slug), and mustSlug validates a slug as lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 1..11 characters, so a symbol's alphabet is [A-Z0-9-] and holds no markdown metacharacter for a sanitiser to act on. THE PREMISE IS PINNED rather than argued: TestACourtSymbolsAlphabetIsWhatMakesItsSanitiserRedundant asserts the alphabet directly, so if slug validation ever widens, that test goes red and this row must be promoted. Kept because the render layer's rule is that user text is sanitised wherever it is printed, and a surface exempted by an upstream invariant should still read like the others - the alternative is a reader having to re-derive the slug charset to know why one call is missing.

label: EnableTestClock: a used realm is refused only if BOTH claims and coin exist
why: UNREACHABLE FROM THIS SUITE BY CONSTRUCTION, and covered by txtar. The usage gate sits behind EnableTestClock's court check, and by the time any gno test runs some earlier test has created a court - so a SUCCESSFUL arming, and therefore the usage gate, cannot be reached here at all. testclock.gno's own scope note says this and names the two txtars that isolate one arm each (this `elsewhere` can hold one path, and the guard checks it resolves, so the second is named here): seeded gives the meta court two claims with the coin supply still zero (and asserts CourtCount()==1, so the count arm is not what refuses), coin does the reverse. Both assert the 'has been used' message from the deployer's own key, which only a txtar can be.

label: EnableTestClock: the disclosure does not outlive sealing
find: tcEverArmed = true         // never cleared again, not even by sealing
why: UNREACHABLE FROM THIS SUITE, and now covered by txtar - it was covered NOWHERE until this row was written. `tcEverArmed = true` is written only by the arming path, which no gno test can complete (a court always exists by then), and every test that reads TestClockFabricated sets the flag BY HAND - so the write itself had no observer. kourtv2_testclock.txtar is the one harness where arming succeeds; it now asserts TestClockFabricated() is true after arming AND still true after sealing. MEASURED: deleting the line fails that script at the new assertion. The sealing half is also held here by TestSealingKeepsTheDisclosure, with the flag set by hand.

label: StakedSize: the address guard is dropped
replace: func StakedSize(courtSlug string, who address) int {
why: INVALID BY MASKING, and the load-bearing half is pinned. StakedSize's `!who.IsValid()` early return cannot change any answer while stakeIdxMine stands: the walk only accepts a key whose length is exactly len(prefix)+8, so a short or malformed `who` matches nothing and the count is 0 with or without the guard, and a `who` of an address's length that is not a real address matches no key either because no such key was ever written. Dropping it therefore reports SURVIVED. MEASURED: dropping it ALONE changes nothing; dropping it TOGETHER with weakening stakeIdxMine to `>=` fails TestNoReadAnswersForANonAddress and TestTheStakeIndexPacksAndOrdersAcrossBuckets - so the pair has teeth and stakeIdxMine is the half that carries them, which its own row pins. Kept because an exported read should refuse junk at its entry rather than rely on a key-length invariant three functions down, and because the same guard in StakedPage is what the junk-input sweep asserts across all eighteen address readers.

label: StakedPage: the read ALLOCATES a position instead of looking one up
replace:
pos := getPos(c, cs, who, side)
			live = pos.stake
			conv = convPreviewCC(cs, pos, acc)
why: CAUGHT BY A GUARD, NOT BY A SUITE, which is what `elsewhere` is for. Replacing the cs.stakers.Get lookup with getPos makes the read ALLOCATE a position on access - the defect the comment on that line names - and no test sees it, because a freshly allocated position reads zero stake and the page prints the same string. check-read-purity.py sees it exactly: `stakeindex.gno:StakedPage calls getPos`, exit 1, measured by applying this row and running the guard. The harness runs suites, so this row will always report SURVIVED there; the annotation names the guard that does the work.

label: EnableTestClock: a realm with one user court may still be armed
why: UNPINNABLE BY THIS SUITE FOR A COUNTING REASON, and the corpus delta pass is what found it. The guard is CourtCount() > 1; widening it to > 2 still REFUSES in the gno suite, because by the time any test runs the realm holds dozens of courts and every small threshold is already exceeded. So a test can assert the refusal - and tcbase_test.gno does - without being able to discriminate the threshold at all. Only a harness holding exactly TWO courts can, and kourtv2_usedrealm_seeded.txtar is that harness: it creates one user court beside meta and asserts the message. MEASURED both ways: the mutation passes the whole kourtv2 suite (44.6s, ok) and fails that txtar at line 123 with `no match for this realm already has courts found in stderr`. This row was recorded as CAUGHT when it was written, on a FILTERED run where only two courts existed - which is exactly the mis-attribution a full pass exists to catch.

label: Minted: the down-correction overshoots, so a buyer is under-minted
why: MASKED BY THE OTHER LOOP, and no single-mutation row can be written. Nudging the down-loop to `cst < coin` makes it step one PAST the answer whenever the payment exactly equals a span's price - and the up-loop immediately repairs it, because Cost(from, s1+1-from) then equals coin, which is not `> coin`, so it steps back. MEASURED: this mutation alone survives every suite; nudging BOTH loops together (`cst < coin` and `cst >= coin`) fails TestMintedIsMaximalAndNeverShortChangesTheBuyer with `paying the exact price of 1 units from 0 minted only 0`, and fails two existing curve tests as well. So the pair has teeth and neither half can be pinned on its own. Kept because a correction loop that stops on the wrong comparison is only correct by the grace of its neighbour. THE PAIR IS NOW PINNED as one row - 'Minted: BOTH correction loops are nudged, so the buyer is short-changed' - because the two loops sit next to each other and a corpus `find` is a text substitution, so the joint mutation needs no more context than the halves did. This row stays as the record of why the HALF survives.

label: Minted: the up-correction stops one short
why: UNREACHABLE, by an argument the arithmetic makes and a probe confirms. The up-loop's `cst > coin` narrowed to `>=` can only matter when the isqrt estimate lands BELOW the true answer AND that answer's cost equals the payment exactly. Those are mutually exclusive: if coin == Cost(from, delta) = ceil((s1^2 - from^2)/2d) with s1 = from+delta, then 2d*coin >= s1^2 - from^2, so from^2 + 2d*coin >= s1^2 and isqrt of that is at least s1 - the estimate is never below the answer at an exact payment. PROBED as well as argued: 4 values of d x 60 starts x 8 spans, zero cases where the estimate undershot at an exact price. Kept because the loop is also the repair for the down-loop's overshoot (see the row above), where the comparison it makes is load-bearing.

label: Cost: the slope is d, not 2d, so every purchase is half price
why: TIMED OUT RATHER THAN CAUGHT, which the harness now says out loud. Halving the slope halves every price, so Minted's correction loops - which walk ONE unit at a time - have to climb through roughly twice the span, and the observer suites ran past SUITE_TIMEOUT. A timeout is a non-result: it is not a catch, and treating it as one would credit the suite with an objection it never made. The mutation is obviously behaviour-changing (every purchase at half price), so this is a cost problem and not a coverage one. IF a bounded variant is wanted, mutate the slope in a way that keeps the loops short - or assert Price/Backing directly, which read d without looping. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 and the status HOLDS: still [timed out] at MUTATE_SUITE_TIMEOUT=120. Note that `make gaps` filters `slow` rows out, and a KNOWN-GAPS row is not in the main corpus either, so this row is measured in NEITHER direction — its status is a claim, not an observation, until somebody re-runs it. To do that: strip `slow` into a scratch batch and run mutate-parallel with MUTATE_SUITE_TIMEOUT set low. Not automated because bounding these needs a PER-ROW timeout — a global 120s would spuriously fail normal rows, one of which timed out at 600s under 4-shard load — and two rows do not justify that plumbing.

label: seriesRowCap: the trim keeps one row more than the cap
why: VALID AND DELIBERATELY UNPINNED. ClaimSeries unions the two capped sides and trims the result with `if len(rows) > seriesRowCap`; narrowing it to `>=` trims a 400-row union to its last 400 - a no-op slice - while setting more = true, so a client is told older change points were dropped when none were. THE OBSTACLE IS THAT A FIXTURE CANNOT PROVE IT HIT THE BOUNDARY. The only observable is the `more` field, and it needs the union to be EXACTLY seriesRowCap; but the intact code trims any union above the cap down to the cap, so a returned count of 400 is ambiguous between 'was 400, untrimmed' and 'was 401+, trimmed'. Counting the output cannot distinguish them, and computing the pre-trim union in the test would restate the production formula this suite keeps single-sited. The emit-side cap IS pinned (see the main-corpus row), so what is unpinned is one wrong boolean on a read whose numbers are all correct. PROMOTE IT if the union size ever becomes observable - a returned pre-trim count, or a trim that reports how many it took.

label: OrderFolders: the input-length bound is exclusive by one
why: VALID BUT NO LEGAL INPUT REACHES THE BOUNDARY. The bound is `len(ids) > maxFolders*21`, sized in the comment for 'a uint64 at its longest plus its separator' - 2,100 bytes. Folder ids are assigned sequentially and maxFolders caps them at 100, so the longest list of ids that RESOLVES is about 400 bytes; an input of exactly 2,100 bytes can only be built from ids that do not exist. So both the intact and the mutated code refuse it, and they differ only in which message comes back - 'that is too long to be a list of folder ids' against the later unknown-folder refusal. Pinnable the same way the transfer amount guards were, by asserting the specific message; not worth a 2,100-byte fixture for a refusal that arrives either way. The bound's PURPOSE - refuse before strings.Split allocates - is unaffected by one byte.

label: Offer: the kind is offered by the REALM, not the caller
why: VALID BUT OBSERVABLE ONLY THROUGH AN EVENT, the same class as PullSenior's zero payment. Governor.Offer uses `who` exactly once, at line 340 - `"offerer", who.String()` inside the emission - and nothing else reads it: a name once offered is bound to its code forever regardless of who offered it. So substituting the realm's own address changes one attribute of one event and no state, and no _test.gno can read events. The filetest `Events:` directive can, but govern's offer path runs through z_offer_filetest.gno whose subject is the offer/adopt flow; asserting an offerer attribute there would pin this. PROMOTE IT if that filetest gains an Events block.

label: mustInvariants: a deploy gate is loosened so it can never fire
why: UNPINNABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and this row stands for the whole class rather than thirteen copies of it. mustInvariants and the tier loop beside it compare CONSTANTS ONLY, at init. Measured: loosening this gate so it can never fire leaves the suite at exit 0 with ZERO failing tests, because the constants satisfy the tighter bound anyway and the gate never fired in the first place. Tightening it instead panics at init, so the realm does not load and the run exits 1 with zero NAMED failures - every test dies and none discriminates, which is a broken measurement rather than a catch. The same argument covers court.gno's other twelve constant gates (the curveCap bounds, the slash-multiple and dispute-arm checks, the 93-way split, the maxBondBps and slashXBps relations, the maxAnswerBondBps drift check, and the meta/ordinary floor loop). Their value is that a future constant change cannot ship silently - which is exactly what a deploy gate is for, and exactly what mutation testing cannot see. It also explains court.gno's low row density: 43 operator lines read as uncovered and most of them are these.

label: dispute: the ride's slash capture moves AFTER the ride (lastFlagEventAt restamp)
why: SURVIVES, and the comment's stated harm is NOT what happens. dispute.gno captures hadSlash before resolveQualityRide and says running both on one tally "would settle the slash in the very call that levied it - burned with no window and no Q5 challenge". It would not: on a JUST-LEVIED slash counterUsed is false, so disposeSlashOnRide takes its !cs.counterUsed case and REARMS rather than settles. The only state that differs is lastFlagEventAt, which originateSlash does not set and rearmSlashWindow does - read by crystallize.gno as the 24h quiet window after the last flag event, so the mutation delays Crystallize by up to a day on the levying-ride path. NOT PROMOTED TO A CAUGHT ROW because Crystallize also requires pendingSlash == 0, and every route to that restamps lastFlagEventAt again, so the difference is plausibly masked before it can be observed - which leaves it undecided between survivor and INVALID, and that is stated rather than guessed. A first attempt replaced `if hadSlash` with a fresh read instead of reordering; that leaves hadSlash declared-and-unused, which gno reports as a TEST error not a build error, so an ad-hoc probe scored it CAUGHT while mutate correctly called it INVALID. For an ordering claim the mutation must reorder.

label: pendingOpenedAt: a stale proposal still bounds the burn
why:
SURVIVES, and the reason recorded here was WRONG TWICE — corrected by measurement rather than re-argued. approveAction discards a proposal older than pendingTTLBlocks and opens a fresh one; this function repeats that test so the burn bound comes from the LIVE proposal rather than a dead one, and DisapproveAllAssociations turns a 0 into heightNow(), which burns every edge instead of sparing those written after a dead proposal opened.

WRONG ONCE: the stated obstacle was 'a SkipHeights that large - the global height is shared across this package and a jump of that size has broken unrelated fixtures here before'. pendingTTLBlocks is flagCooldownBlocks is 120_960, which is EXACTLY 168 epochs of 720, so the skip is phase-neutral; and this suite already performs 120 skips of votingBlocks+1 = 120_961. A skip of that size is routine here, not a hazard.

WRONG TWICE, and this is the real obstacle: the sketch 'it needs a signature, then a wait of flagCooldownBlocks, then a second signature' DOES NOT REACH THE BRANCH. approveAction ends a firing act with pending.Remove(key), so no entry survives a fire; and when it meets a stale entry it sets a = nil and opens a fresh proposal carrying only the current signer. So the second signature fires only when m == 1, and at m >= 2 the live entry at read time is always FRESH — clean and mutant agree and nothing is observable. The one sequence that does reach it: open at m >= 2, let the TTL elapse, add a bonded edge, LOWER m to 1, then sign. Clean reads 0 and burns the new edge; the mutant reads the dead proposal's height and spares it.

STILL NOT FIXED, deliberately: that sequence needs the m-of-n threshold lowered between the two calls, which is a legitimate governance move but a contrived fixture, and association.gno is a day old with its author actively extending the subsystem (standing.gno). A fixture keyed to today's bulk-burn semantics would likely be rewritten before it earned anything. The difficulty is now stated correctly, which is what the next attempt needed.
